findings.source_quote: ὅτι καλαὶ καὶ δυναταὶ καὶ ἱλαραὶ καὶ ἔνδοξοι καὶ δυνάμεναι σῶσαι ψυχὴν ἀνθρώπου
findings.english_quote: that they are good and powerful and gladdening and glorious and able to save a person’s soul
findings.issue: “Powerful” presents δυναταί as an assertion of the commandments’ power rather than their practicability. In this passage, doubt about following the commandments is answered by promises of strengthening and ability to keep them. “Possible to keep” makes that contextual sense explicit and distinguishes it from the following assertion that the commandments can save a person’s soul. Although δυνατός can express power elsewhere, the supplied wording does not preserve the feasibility sense supported here.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “that they are good and possible to keep and gladdening and glorious and able to save a person’s soul.” Review this proposed wording afresh before adoption.

findings.source_quote: ὅτι καλαὶ καὶ δυναταὶ καὶ ἱλαραὶ καὶ ἔνδοξοι καὶ δυνάμεναι σῶσαι ψυχὴν ἀνθρώπου
findings.english_quote: they are good and powerful, they bring joy, they are glorious, and they can save a person’s soul
findings.issue: Independently of the standard edition, “powerful” fails to communicate the contextual practicability of the commandments expressed by δυναταί. The ensuing discussion concerns whether people can follow and keep them; their capacity to save is separately expressed by δυνάμεναι σῶσαι.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “they are good and can be kept, they bring joy, they are glorious, and they can save a person’s soul.” Review this proposed wording afresh before adoption.

findings.source_quote: αὗται αἱ ἐντολαὶ σύμφοροί εἰσι τοῖς μέλλουσι μετανοεῖν· ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ πορευθῶσιν ἐν αὐταῖς, εἰς μάτην ἐστὶν ἡ μετάνοια αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: These commandments help those who are about to repent[a]. But if they do not live by them, their repentance is useless.
findings.issue: “But” substitutes an adversative relationship for explanatory γάρ. The source gives the futility of repentance without following the commandments as the explanation for their benefit, not as a contrasting qualification. The conditional and its negation are otherwise retained.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “These commandments help those who are about to repent[a], because if they do not live by them, their repentance is useless.” Review the replacement for readability and fidelity before adoption.

summary: Both editions cover all supplied clauses and preserve the principal conditions, negations, speakers, and contextual repentance terminology. Both retain brackets around the source’s bracketed “all,” rather than presenting it as unqualified preserved text. Revision is recommended for δυναταί in both editions and for the lost explanatory connection in the simplified edition. This review concerns the supplied working source and English materials only; it does not authenticate manuscripts, certify unseen editions, or establish a uniquely possible interpretation.
